runtime_build_track.spec_requested: Primary track: source-controlled builds at the exact pinned commits (Bun 8326d1bd39a96f1f298c3de195aad15972d4f3b4, Node ad7a5b8302ae54b6e6dc77e03eabc5a3218dfb85).
runtime_build_track.actual_track_used: RELEASE BUILDS for BOTH runtimes (documented deviation).
runtime_build_track.deviation_reason: Attempted to build Bun from source at the pinned commit. Bun's rust-toolchain.toml requires Rust nightly-2026-07-20. `rustup toolchain install` failed: `error downloading file from 'https://static.rust-lang.org/dist/2026-07-20/channel-rust-nightly.toml.sha256' ... tunnel error: unsuccessful`. Verified independently via direct curl: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://static.rust-lang.org/` returned `000` (hard connection failure, not an HTTP-level error). This is a real, verified environmental network restriction in this sandbox, not an assumption. Because a from-source Bun build was infeasible, the release-build track was used for BOTH Bun and Node (same consistent track on both sides of the comparison), matching the approach already used and user-approved for H4 and H6.

runtime_build_track.IMPORTANT_verified_source_vs_binary_dive: Per the H5 protocol's explicit instruction ('do not assume that a source pin means the binary actually corresponds to that commit without verifying it'), the pinned Node commit's lib/buffer.js was checked against the actual behavior of the benchmarked v22.22.2 binary, and a real, concrete divergence was found: the pinned commit's source sets `Buffer.poolSize = 64 * 1024` (65536, i.e. a 64KB pool with a 32KB pooling threshold at `size < poolSize>>>1`), but the installed v22.22.2 binary was empirically verified (see 'node_pooling_verification' below) to use `Buffer.poolSize = 8192` (8KB pool, 4KB threshold) — the long-standing Node default, not the pinned commit's value. This means the pinned commit is NOT representative of the poolSize/threshold constants actually exercised by the benchmarked binary, even though the underlying POOLING MECHANISM (branch on `size < threshold` -> slice from a shared pool vs. `createUnsafeBuffer` fresh allocation) is structurally the same in both. All quantitative interpretation below uses the EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED v22.22.2 threshold (4096 bytes), not the pinned commit's constant.

node_pooling_verification.method: Directly probed the benchmarked v22.22.2 binary's actual Buffer behavior rather than trusting source-read constants alone.
node_pooling_verification.empirical_test: Allocated 5 consecutive Buffer.allocUnsafe(size) buffers per size and compared `.buffer` (underlying ArrayBuffer) identity across them.

results.4096: NOT pooled (0/4 shared; each gets its own 4096-byte ArrayBuffer)
results.4097: NOT pooled (0/4 shared; each gets its own 4097-byte ArrayBuffer)
results.16384: NOT pooled (0/4 shared; each gets its own 16384-byte ArrayBuffer)

node_pooling_verification.conclusion: Confirms the pooling threshold on the ACTUAL benchmarked binary is exactly 4096 bytes (size < 4096 -> pooled; size >= 4096 -> fresh allocation), consistent with `size < (Buffer.poolSize >>> 1)` where Buffer.poolSize=8192. This places 3 of the 6 tested sizes (16, 64, 256, 1024) inside the pooled regime and 2 sizes (4096, 16384) outside it, with size=256... wait size=1024 also inside. See results/README.md for the resulting performance pattern.

bun_pooling_verification.method: Same empirical ArrayBuffer-identity probe applied to the benchmarked Bun 1.3.13 binary.
bun_pooling_verification.results_all_sizes_tested: 16, 64, 1024, 4096, 16384: 0/4 pooled at every size — every Buffer.allocUnsafe() call returns a distinct, freshly-sized ArrayBuffer.
bun_pooling_verification.conclusion: Confirms Bun performs NO pooling at any tested size — consistent with source-read (src/jsc/bindings/JSBuffer.cpp: jsBufferConstructorFunction_allocUnsafeBody unconditionally calls createUninitializedBuffer() -> JSC::JSUint8Array::createUninitialized(), no pool/threshold branch).

background_workload.description: Same shared sandbox as H4/H6. No HTTP load generator or database server running concurrently for H5 (unlike H4/H6) — each timed run is a single short-lived child process launched via /usr/bin/time -v, measured via in-process process.hrtime.bigint(), not network round-trips. This reduces (but does not eliminate) exposure to host-level noise.
other_processes_running: session management processes (claude CLI, environment-manager) — low, roughly constant CPU usage, present identically across all runs

warmup.chunking: 10 chunks during warmup phase, timed individually via process.hrtime.bigint()
warmup.stability_check_predefined_before_any_ru: Compare mean per-chunk time of last half of chunks vs first half. Stable if |relative_change| <= 0.15 AND CV of last-half chunk timings <= 0.25. This exact rule was written into orchestrate.py's chunk_stability_check() BEFORE the experiment was executed and was NOT modified after seeing results.
warmup.outcome: Only 2 of 12 runtime x size combos (bun-64, bun-1024) reached the declared STABLE state within the bounded extensions; the other 10 combos hit UNSTABLE_AFTER_MAX_EXTENSIONS at 400,000 warmup iterations (8x the starting 50,000). See results/README.md 'Surprising findings' and 'Data-quality assessment' for full disclosure and interpretation — this is reported as a genuine methodological finding, not hidden or silently patched.

timed_runs.wrapper: /usr/bin/time -v <runtime> alloc-bench.js <size> 1000000 4096 timed — used to capture Maximum resident set size (peak RSS) per run in addition to alloc-bench.js's own process.hrtime.bigint()-based throughput measurement.

gc_instrumentation_note: GC activity/pause counters were NOT collected in the main timed runs. Node exposes --expose-gc/perf_hooks GC instrumentation; Bun's GC is JSC-based with different instrumentation. Rather than force a comparison on non-equivalent counters (which the H5 protocol explicitly cautioned against), this was omitted from the primary measurement and is disclosed as a limitation, not silently worked around.
